therapeutic_hypothesis.claimed_target: multiple (GABA-A receptor, H1 receptor, D2 receptor)
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: suppression of nausea and vomiting reflex
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change in numeric rating scale (NRS) for self-reported nausea from baseline to 60 minutes after topical application

results.effect_size: Mean difference 0.8 points on 0–10 NRS (ABH 1.70 vs placebo 0.90)

context.indication: nausea and vomiting in cancer patients
context.investigator_commentary: A crossover design was used with two sequences: ABH then placebo, or placebo then ABH. No carry-over effect was assumed. A paired t-test and repeated measures analysis were used. The mean NRS reduction was 1.70 for ABH gel and 0.90 for placebo, with a mean difference of 0.8; no statistically significant p-value was reported.

results_by_chain.endpoint: Change in NRS nausea score at 60 minutes
results_by_chain.mechanism_description: receptor antagonism at GABA-A, histamine H1, and dopamine D2 receptors
results_by_chain.biology_description: suppression of nausea and vomiting reflex
results_by_chain.population_description: cancer patients with active nausea receiving topical ABH gel first then placebo
